cosmology.comovingDistance: Simpson, 512 intervals over [0, z], matching Core/Scale/Cosmology.ComovingDistanceMpc

note: Every distance here is comoving, from the redshift, at the cosmology above. Basin attractors are reconstruction products; cluster positions are measured and their distances are not.

places.name: Laniakea
places.reference: Dupuy & Courtois 2023, Cosmicflows-4 basins of attraction, Table A.1; values transcribed from docs/research/2026-09-11-data-beyond-and-cmb.md section 4.3, which read them from the paper PDF
places.description: The attractor (or repeller) of a gravitational basin in the Cosmicflows-4 velocity reconstruction. It is a property of a reconstructed field, not an object that can be observed at this position. CosmoSynth ships this point and this published volume, and does NOT ship the basin boundary: the watershed grid that defines it is Cosmicflows-4 data, which carries no commercial licence (docs/DATA-LICENCE-AMENDMENT.md section 3). A boundary drawn without that grid would be invented, so there is none.

places.name: Bootes Void
places.reference: NAME Bootes Void; position resolved through CDS SIMBAD, 2026-09-12; redshift is SIMBAD's. The redshift is INFERRED
places.description: No sphere in lss/voids.cspt is labelled with this name. VoidFinder partitions this region into several smaller voids, none of which is the ~60 Mpc object the name usually denotes, so naming a catalogue row after it would be a wrong claim dressed as data.
